Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns every system-rule change that enforces SFIP stand-alone issuance and the 60-day proof-of-loss clock in the admin platforms; escalates scope conflicts to Head of IT.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 44 CFR 62.23(i)(1) and the NFIP Claims Manual (June 2025 edition) re-read against the FEMA Flood Handbook postings at each configuration change; SFIP Homeowner Flood Form language (89 FR 8272; proposed 44 CFR 61 App A(4)) checked for endorsement prohibitions.

In-scope processes.value: Policy issuance rule engine (block SFIP being added as an endorsement to any non-flood policy) and claims intake/adjustment timers (60-day proof-of-loss deadline, NFIP Claims Manual adjustment codes) across Policy Administration Platform and Guidewire ClaimCenter.

In-scope systems.value: Policy Administration Platform underwriting rule engine; Guidewire ClaimCenter claim-timer and adjustment-code configuration; changes tracked in the CMDB.

Compliance procedure documented.value: NFIP System Configuration Control Procedure — trigger, rule mapping, build, UAT, CAB approval, deploy, post-deployment verification.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Head of IT and Head of Compliance; re-approved on every NFIP Claims Manual bulletin or WYO Arrangement amendment.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Configuration changes triggered by a Claims Manual bulletin must be live before the bulletin's stated effective date; the in-system 60-day proof-of-loss timer and the 60-days-after-loss adjustment window are hard-coded, non-overridable fields.

Deadline reminders configured.value: ClaimCenter fires adjuster queue alerts at day 45 and day 55 of an open claim missing proof of loss, and auto-flags the file at day 60.

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Configuration change tickets, UAT scripts, CAB approval and post-deployment verification screenshots retained 7 years from the rule's retirement in the compliance evidence repository.

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Configuration defects (e.g., a state allowing SFIP endorsement, a missing timer) are logged as ITSM incidents with severity, root cause and fix-forward date.

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of IT signs off on every configuration defect fix before the ticket is closed.

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All NFIP-tagged configuration change tickets closed in the quarter across Policy Administration Platform and Guidewire ClaimCenter.

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any live rule permitting SFIP issuance by endorsement, or any claim missing the 60-day proof-of-loss timer, is a fail.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per-change; test runs quarterly over that quarter's closed-change population plus 100% of changes touching the proof-of-loss timer.

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer did not build or peer-review the sampled configuration change.

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly configuration-test workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Change tickets, UAT evidence and CMDB extract, presentable to FEMA/NFIP Bureau within 5 business days of request.

Regulator response path.value: Head of IT coordinates the technical response; Regulatory Reporting Manager clears the response to FEMA/NFIP before it is sent.

checklist.step: Intake the triggering rule change and open a configuration ticket
actions: Read the triggering source — an NFIP Claims Manual bulletin, a WYO Financial Assistance/Subsidy Arrangement amendment, or an SFIP form revision (e.g., 89 FR 8272) — and identify the exact rule text that changed.
In the ITSM platform open Change ▸ New Change Request, tag Category = 'NFIP/Flood' and paste the bulletin or Federal Register citation into the description.
Ask the Regulatory Filing Specialist to confirm the rule's effective date and whether it applies to new business only or new + in-force.
Attach the source bulletin/citation PDF to the change ticket.
checklist.done: the change ticket carries the source citation, effective date and in-force/new-business scope.

checklist.step: Map the rule to the exact system field or timer it must control
actions: In Policy Administration Platform open the product configuration workbench for the flood/SFIP product and locate the policy-type and endorsement-eligibility fields.
In Guidewire ClaimCenter open Administration ▸ Claim Rules and locate the proof-of-loss timer and the NFIP Claims Manual adjustment-code list.
Document on the ticket the exact field/rule ID, its current value and the required new value.
Confirm with the Claims Director / Manager that the mapped ClaimCenter rule matches how adjusters actually work the file.
checklist.done: the ticket names the exact field/rule ID in each system and the before/after values.

checklist.step: Configure Policy Administration Platform to block SFIP issuance by endorsement
actions: In the product configuration workbench, set the flood/SFIP product's issuance rule so the SFIP can only be created as a stand-alone policy transaction, never attached as an endorsement to a homeowners, dwelling or commercial policy.
Add a hard-stop validation message referencing 44 CFR 62.23(i)(1) that fires if an underwriter attempts to endorse flood coverage onto another policy.
Save the configuration to the lower (test) environment and record the build ID on the ticket.
checklist.done: the lower environment shows the SFIP stand-alone hard-stop live and the build ID is logged.

checklist.step: Configure ClaimCenter's proof-of-loss timer and Claims Manual adjustment codes
actions: In Administration ▸ Claim Rules, set the proof-of-loss due-date field to date-of-loss + 60 days, non-editable by adjusters.
Load the current NFIP Claims Manual (June 2025) adjustment-code table into the claim activity picklist so adjusters cannot select a retired code.
Configure the day-45 and day-55 queue alerts and the day-60 file flag referenced in the generic answers.
Save to the lower environment and record the build ID.
checklist.done: the lower environment enforces the 60-day timer and the current Claims Manual codes, with alerts configured.

checklist.step: Peer-review the build against the ticket's field mapping
actions: Compare the lower-environment configuration in both systems field-by-field against the ticket's before/after values.
Confirm no unrelated fields were changed by diffing the configuration export against the prior version.
Sign the peer-review checklist and attach it to the ticket.
checklist.done: the peer review is signed and the diff shows only the intended fields changed.

checklist.step: Execute UAT scripts proving the rule fires correctly
actions: Run a test case attempting to add SFIP coverage as an endorsement to a test homeowners policy in Policy Administration Platform and confirm the hard-stop fires with the correct citation message.
Run a test case creating a flood claim in ClaimCenter with a loss date 61 days in the past and confirm the file auto-flags at day 60.
Run a negative test confirming a retired Claims Manual adjustment code cannot be selected.
Attach the UAT script results and screenshots to the ticket.
checklist.done: all UAT scripts pass and evidence is attached to the ticket.

checklist.step: Take the change through Change Advisory Board approval
actions: Present the ticket, UAT evidence and peer review at the CAB session, referencing the citation and the effective date deadline.
Record the CAB approval decision and any conditions on the ticket.
Schedule the production deployment window ahead of the rule's effective date.
checklist.done: CAB approval is recorded on the ticket with a scheduled deployment date that beats the effective date.

checklist.step: Deploy the configuration to production
actions: Deploy the approved configuration package to Policy Administration Platform and Guidewire ClaimCenter production during the scheduled window.
Confirm the deployment log shows both systems on the new build ID.
Notify the Configuration Engineer that deployment completed.
checklist.done: production shows both systems on the approved build ID.

checklist.step: Verify the live rule in production
actions: Re-run the SFIP endorsement hard-stop and the 60-day claim-flag test in the production environment using a controlled test policy/claim, then delete the test records per data-handling procedure.
Screenshot the passing results and attach them to the ticket.
Update the CMDB configuration item record with the new build ID and effective date.
checklist.done: production verification screenshots are attached and the CMDB record is updated.

checklist.step: Notify downstream owners the rule is live
actions: Email the Claims Director / Manager and Policy Admin Ops Lead confirming the effective date and what changed.
Notify the Compliance Manager so the training content in the WYO handling-requirements training item can be updated to reflect the new rule.
Post the change summary to the team's Confluence release-notes page.
checklist.done: downstream owners and the Compliance Manager have written confirmation the rule is live.

checklist.step: Log any configuration exception
actions: If UAT or production verification fails, open an incident ticket with severity, the specific field that failed, and root cause.
Assign a fix-forward owner and a re-test date.
Escalate to Head of IT if the failure risks a missed regulatory effective date.
checklist.done: any failure is logged as an incident with owner, root cause and re-test date.

checklist.step: Retain the configuration record
actions: File the ticket, peer review, UAT evidence, CAB approval and production verification screenshots into the compliance evidence repository under the rule's citation and effective date.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
checklist.done: the full configuration record is filed and retention-labelled in the repository.

checklist.step: Reconcile the CMDB against the live rule set quarterly
actions: Export the CMDB's NFIP-tagged configuration items and compare each to the live production rule value.
Flag and correct any CMDB record that has drifted from the live system.
checklist.done: the CMDB matches the live system for every NFIP-tagged configuration item.

checklist.step: Re-validate the rule set on every Claims Manual bulletin
actions: On each new NFIP Claims Manual bulletin, re-read the change against the live adjustment-code table and timer values.
Open a new change ticket if a discrepancy is found, repeating the configuration build/test/deploy steps.
checklist.done: every bulletin is checked against the live configuration within 10 business days of publication.

checklist.step: Report configuration status to the compliance program
actions: Prepare a monthly status summary of open, deployed and failed NFIP configuration changes.
Send it to the Compliance Manager for inclusion in the WYO oversight reporting pack.
checklist.done: the monthly configuration status summary reaches the Compliance Manager.

testing.step: Build the population of NFIP configuration changes for the quarter
actions: Extract every ticket tagged Category = 'NFIP/Flood' closed in the quarter from the ITSM platform.
Reconcile the extract count to the CAB meeting minutes for the same period.
Resolve any count difference with the Change Coordinator before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to CAB minutes and signed as complete.

actions: Take 100% of tickets that touched the SFIP endorsement rule or the proof-of-loss timer.
Take a random sample of 10 additional tickets from the remaining population.
Record the seed and population size in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn and reproducible, covering all timer/endorsement-rule tickets.

actions: Re-read the source bulletin/citation for each sampled ticket and independently determine the field/rule that should have changed.
Compare to what the ticket recorded; any mismatch is an exception.
testing.done: each sampled ticket has an independent mapping note and any mismatch is logged.

testing.step: Re-run the UAT scripts against production
actions: For each sampled ticket, re-run the same SFIP endorsement hard-stop or 60-day claim-flag test directly in production (or the nearest refresh environment).
Capture screenshots of the result and compare to the original UAT evidence.
testing.done: each sampled rule is independently confirmed live and behaving as configured.

testing.step: Verify CAB approval and deployment timing
actions: Confirm CAB approval exists and pre-dates the production deployment for each sampled ticket.
Confirm the deployment date is on or before the rule's regulatory effective date.
testing.done: no sampled change deployed after its regulatory effective date, and CAB approval pre-dates deployment.

testing.step: Trace the CMDB record to the live system
actions: For each sampled ticket, compare the CMDB configuration-item value to the live production value.
Log any drift as an exception.
testing.done: the CMDB agrees with production for every sampled ticket, or the drift is logged.

actions: Confirm the ticket, peer review, UAT evidence, CAB approval and production verification are all filed in the repository for each sampled ticket.
Confirm the 7-year retention label is applied.
testing.done: every sampled ticket's evidence set is complete and retention-labelled.

testing.step: Test the exception log for unresolved defects
actions: Pull all incident tickets raised against NFIP configuration changes in the period.
Confirm each has an owner, root cause and closed re-test, or is still open with a current target date.
testing.done: no incident ticket is stale without an owner or target date.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each testing exception with the ticket id, what was missed and the compliance impact.
Assign root cause and an owner with a remediation date.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for endorsement/timer rules.
Write the conclusion with evidence references and have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual NFIP/WYO handling-requirements training curriculum and the pass-rate that keeps the company eligible to write and re-enter the WYO Program.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 44 CFR 62.23(i)(2)-(3) (adjuster authorization/Flood Control Number), 44 CFR Part 59/60 (floodplain criteria) and 44 CFR 62.24(c) (WYO participation criteria) re-read against the current NFIP Claims Manual and TRRP Plan editions before each annual cycle.

In-scope processes.value: Annual training and competency sign-off for every claims adjuster, policy administration and accounting staff member who touches NFIP flood business, plus TRRP monthly output-tape/financial-statement preparers.

In-scope systems.value: Course delivery, quiz scoring and completion tracking in the learning management system; training content sourced from the current NFIP Claims Manual and TRRP Plan documentation.

Compliance procedure documented.value: NFIP/WYO Staff Training Procedure — curriculum content, audience mapping, annual delivery window, competency test, remediation for failures.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Head of Compliance; curriculum refreshed annually and on any NFIP Claims Manual or TRRP Plan bulletin.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual cycle must close before the WYO Arrangement renewal date; new hires in an in-scope role must complete training within 30 days of start.

Deadline reminders configured.value: LMS auto-reminders at 60/30/10 days before the annual cycle close date to managers of incomplete staff.

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Course rosters, quiz scores and completion certificates retained 5 years in the learning management system and mirrored to the compliance evidence repository.

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Staff who do not complete or pass the competency test by the deadline are suspended from NFIP-touching transactions and logged with a remediation date.

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Compliance Manager signs off once a suspended staff member re-tests and passes.

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All staff flagged in the HRIS as holding an NFIP-touching role during the training year.

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% completion and a zero-error-tolerance pass on the Flood Control Number/adjuster-authorization module, mirroring the TRRP zero-error standard; any staff member below threshold is a fail.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Tested annually at cycle close, aligned to the training obligation's own annual frequency.

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer did not design or deliver the training content.

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual training-test workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.

Regulator-ready documentation.value: LMS completion export mapped to the HRIS role roster, produced within 5 business days of a FEMA/state exam request.

Regulator response path.value: Compliance Manager owns the exam response; Head of Compliance clears it before submission.

checklist.step: Identify the in-scope population from HRIS role tags
actions: Pull the roster of claims adjusters, policy administration and accounting staff tagged as NFIP-touching in the HRIS.
Cross-check the roster against the org chart with the Claims Director / Manager.
Flag new hires within the last 30 days.
Hand the confirmed list to the Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: the roster of in-scope staff is confirmed complete against the org chart.

checklist.step: Refresh curriculum content against current NFIP Claims Manual and TRRP Plan
actions: Pull the current NFIP Claims Manual (June 2025) and TRRP Plan documentation.
Diff the new content against last year's course material.
Update modules covering adjuster authorization/Flood Control Number rules (44 CFR 62.23(i)(2)-(3)) and Part 59/60 floodplain criteria.
Route the updated slides to Regulatory Counsel for a citation check.
checklist.done: the curriculum is updated and citation-checked against current source documents.

checklist.step: Build or refresh the course and competency quiz in the LMS
actions: In the LMS course-authoring tool, create or update the 'NFIP WYO Handling Requirements' course.
Build a quiz bank testing Flood Control Number assignment, 60-day proof-of-loss handling and TRRP output-tape field standards.
Set the pass threshold to 100% on the Flood Control Number/adjuster-authorization module.
Publish the course to the assigned-learner group.
checklist.done: the course and quiz are published in the LMS with the pass threshold set.

checklist.step: Assign the course to every in-scope staff member
actions: Bulk-assign the course to the HRIS-sourced roster in the LMS assignment screen.
Set the due date ahead of the WYO Arrangement renewal date.
Configure the assignment group to auto-sync new hires.
checklist.done: 100% of the in-scope roster shows an assigned, due-dated course.

checklist.step: Deliver instructor-led sessions for adjusters and accounting
actions: Schedule live sessions covering NFIP Claims Manual adjustment standards and WYO Accounting Procedures Manual ledger separation.
Record attendance in the LMS session log.
Record the session and post it in the LMS for staff who could not attend live.
checklist.done: attendance is logged in the LMS for every scheduled session.

checklist.step: Track completion against the due date
actions: Run the LMS completion dashboard weekly during the cycle.
Identify staff below 100% progress.
Escalate incomplete staff to their manager via Microsoft Teams / Email.
checklist.done: weekly completion tracking is documented with escalations sent for incomplete staff.

checklist.step: Administer the competency quiz and score it
actions: Release the quiz only after course-module completion.
Auto-score the quiz in the LMS.
Flag any score below 100% on the Flood Control Number module for remediation.
checklist.done: every completer has a recorded quiz score, and sub-threshold scores are flagged.

checklist.step: Remediate failed or incomplete staff
actions: Assign a remediation session and a re-test within 10 business days.
Request the Claims Director / Manager suspend the staff member from NFIP-touching transactions in the interim.
Document the suspension and lift dates.
checklist.done: every failed or incomplete staff member has a remediation date and, if suspended, a documented lift date.

checklist.step: Confirm the suspension is enforced in the operating system
actions: Verify the suspended staff member's NFIP transaction permissions are disabled in Policy Administration Platform / ClaimCenter until remediation clears.
Re-enable access only on the Compliance Manager's written clearance.
checklist.done: system access reflects the suspension and is re-enabled only on written clearance.

checklist.step: Close the annual cycle and generate the completion report
actions: Export the final completion/pass report from the LMS.
Reconcile the count to the original HRIS roster.
Note any residual gaps and their remediation date.
checklist.done: the closed-cycle report reconciles to the HRIS roster with no unexplained gaps.

checklist.step: Certify training status supports WYO Arrangement renewal
actions: Review the closed-cycle completion report.
Sign a certification memo confirming staff readiness ahead of the WYO Arrangement renewal filing.
Send the memo to the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
checklist.done: a signed certification memo is delivered ahead of the WYO renewal filing.

checklist.step: Log exceptions with disposition
actions: Log any staff member who never completed the cycle as an exception with root cause and disposition (role change, leave, termination).
Retain the disposition note in the repository.
checklist.done: every non-completion has a logged disposition.

checklist.step: Retain training evidence
actions: Export rosters, quiz scores and certificates from the LMS.
File the evidence in the compliance evidence repository under the training year.
Apply the 5-year retention label.
checklist.done: the full evidence set is filed and retention-labelled.

checklist.step: Add the module to new-hire onboarding
actions: Add the NFIP WYO course to the new-hire onboarding checklist for in-scope roles.
Confirm the 30-day completion rule is enforced by an HRIS workflow gate.
checklist.done: the onboarding checklist enforces the 30-day completion rule for new hires.

checklist.step: Report training status to the compliance program
actions: Prepare a summary of completion rate, quiz pass rate and open exceptions.
Present the summary to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting.
checklist.done: the summary reaches the Compliance Committee.

actions: Extract the HRIS roster of NFIP-touching roles as of cycle close.
Reconcile the roster to the LMS assignment list.
Resolve differences with the Compliance Manager before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled between HRIS and LMS.

actions: Take 100% of staff who failed or were suspended.
Take a random sample of 15 additional completers.
testing.done: the sample is drawn covering all failures.

actions: For each sampled staff member, pull the LMS transcript.
Confirm the completion date and quiz score match the closed-cycle report.
testing.done: the transcript matches the report for every sampled record, or an exception is logged.

actions: For sampled failures, confirm a remediation date and a re-test result exist.
Where suspended, confirm system access was disabled for the suspension window.
testing.done: remediation and suspension are evidenced for every sampled failure.

testing.step: Re-perform a quiz question against current source
actions: Pick 5 competency-quiz questions.
Verify the correct answer against the current NFIP Claims Manual/TRRP Plan text.
testing.done: all sampled questions match current source text or are flagged for content update.

actions: Sample 5 new hires in in-scope roles.
Confirm course completion within 30 days of start date.
testing.done: all sampled new hires met the 30-day rule or are logged as exceptions.

actions: Confirm the Head of Compliance certification memo pre-dates the WYO Arrangement renewal filing date.
testing.done: the memo pre-dates the renewal filing.

actions: Confirm rosters, scores and certificates are filed and retention-labelled for the sampled population.
testing.done: evidence is complete and labelled for every sampled record.

actions: Raise an issue for each exception with root cause and owner.
Set a remediation date.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, owner and remediation date.

actions: Compute the completion/pass rate against the 100% threshold.
Write the conclusion; have the independent reviewer sign.
Report results to the Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper is filed and reported.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns intake, tracking and root-cause remediation of every flood-policyholder complaint, including those routed through FEMA/NFIP channels.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 44 CFR Part 59/60 general provisions, 44 CFR 62.23(i) WYO customer-service standards and 44 CFR 62.24(c) participation criteria re-read at each policy refresh.

In-scope processes.value: Complaint intake (direct, state DOI referral, FEMA/NFIP referral), classification, investigation, response and root-cause remediation for all NFIP flood business.

In-scope systems.value: Complaint case management in the workflow/case management tool; intake also captured via the Customer Self-Service Portal and Contact Center.

Compliance procedure documented.value: Flood Complaint Handling Procedure — intake channels, classification taxonomy, response SLA, FEMA referral handling, root-cause and remediation logging.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Head of Compliance; reviewed annually.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Each complaint is tracked to the state's required response window (commonly 10-20 business days) and to any FEMA/NFIP-specified inquiry response date.

Deadline reminders configured.value: The case management tool alerts the assigned Complaints Specialist at 50% and 80% of the response window elapsed.

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Complaint log, correspondence and resolution notes retained 5 years and available to FEMA on request.

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Complaints closed past the response window or missing a root-cause code are logged as exceptions.

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Sign-off required on every root-cause remediation action before the case is closed.

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All flood-tagged complaint cases opened or closed in the quarter in the case management tool, including FEMA/NFIP-referred cases.

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance for missed response windows on FEMA-referred complaints; 5% or lower missed-window rate on all other complaints.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Continuous obligation tested monthly against the rolling open/closed case population.

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer did not handle any sampled complaint.

Evidence location for test results.value: Monthly complaint-test workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Complaint log export with root-cause codes and resolution dates, producible within 5 business days for a FEMA Financial Control Plan review or state exam.

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager owns the response; General Counsel clears any admission of a missed deadline.

checklist.step: Capture every complaint at first point of contact
actions: Log complaints received via the portal, Contact Center, mail or state DOI referral into the workflow/case management tool the same business day.
Capture policy number, Flood Control Number, complaint category and channel.
Confirm the complainant receives a written acknowledgment.
checklist.done: every complaint is logged same-day with policy/Flood Control Number and channel.

checklist.step: Classify the complaint against the flood-specific taxonomy
actions: Tag the category: claims handling, premium/billing, policy issuance or service.
Tag whether it was FEMA/NFIP-referred.
Route claims-handling complaints to the Claims Director / Manager for input.
checklist.done: every complaint has a category tag and a routing decision recorded.

checklist.step: Set the response-window clock
actions: Identify the applicable state's response-window requirement, or the FEMA-specified date for a referred inquiry.
Set the case due date in the tool.
Confirm the 50%/80% alert triggers are active on the case.
checklist.done: every case has a due date and active alerts.

checklist.step: Investigate the underlying facts
actions: Pull the policy file from Policy Administration Platform and, where claims-related, the claim file from Guidewire ClaimCenter.
Interview the handling adjuster or underwriter.
Document the investigation findings on the case.
checklist.done: the case file documents the facts investigated and their source.

checklist.step: Draft and clear the response
actions: Draft the written response addressing each point raised.
Route the draft to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager for review.
Route to General Counsel if the complaint alleges a regulatory violation.
checklist.done: the response is reviewed and, where required, cleared by counsel before sending.

checklist.step: Send the response within the tracked window
actions: Send the response via the same channel the complaint arrived on.
Log the send date in the case management tool.
Confirm the send date beats the due date set earlier.
checklist.done: the response is sent and the send date is on or before the due date.

checklist.step: Route FEMA/NFIP-referred complaints to the correct channel
actions: Confirm the FEMA/NFIP referral reference number is recorded on the case.
Respond through the FEMA-specified channel.
Copy the Regulatory Reporting Manager on the response.
checklist.done: FEMA-referred complaints carry the referral number and a response through the correct channel.

checklist.step: Code the root cause
actions: Assign a root-cause code at case close: claims handling error, communication gap, system defect, agent error, or policy misunderstanding.
Link the code to the investigation notes.
checklist.done: every closed case carries a root-cause code linked to its investigation notes.

checklist.step: Identify complaints requiring remediation beyond the individual case
actions: Review root-cause codes weekly for clusters (3 or more complaints, same code, same product/state within 90 days).
Open a remediation item for any cluster found.
checklist.done: clusters are identified weekly and a remediation item exists for each.

checklist.step: Drive the remediation to closure
actions: Assign the remediation item to the accountable process owner (e.g., Claims Director / Manager, or Configuration Engineer for a system defect).
Set a target date and track to completion.
checklist.done: every remediation item has an owner, target date and completion status.

checklist.step: Verify the fix actually resolved the root cause
actions: Monitor the complaint category for 90 days post-remediation.
Confirm the cluster does not recur.
checklist.done: a 90-day post-remediation check is documented showing the cluster did not recur, or further action is opened.

checklist.step: Maintain the complaint log for FEMA/state availability
actions: Export the full complaint log monthly.
Confirm all required fields are populated.
File the export in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: a complete monthly complaint log export is filed and field-complete.

checklist.step: Log exceptions with disposition
actions: For any case that missed its response window or lacks a root-cause code, log an exception with cause and disposition.
checklist.done: every exception is logged with cause and disposition.

checklist.step: Report complaint trends to Market Conduct leadership
actions: Prepare a monthly complaint-trend summary by category, root cause and response-window performance.
Present the summary to the Compliance Committee.
checklist.done: the monthly trend summary reaches the Compliance Committee.

checklist.step: Retain complaint records per requirement
actions: Apply the 5-year retention label to closed cases.
Confirm searchability by policy number and Flood Control Number.
checklist.done: closed cases are retention-labelled and searchable.

actions: Extract all flood-tagged complaints opened/closed in the quarter.
Reconcile the count to the monthly log exports.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the monthly exports.

actions: Take 100% of FEMA/NFIP-referred complaints.
Take a random sample of 20 additional complaints.
testing.done: the sample is drawn covering all FEMA-referred cases.

actions: For each sampled case, recompute the due date from the applicable state/FEMA rule.
Compare the recomputed due date to the actual send date.
testing.done: timing is recomputed and compared for every sampled case.

actions: Confirm each sampled case's response addresses every point raised.
Trace the response back to the policy/claim file referenced.
testing.done: response completeness is verified against the source file for every sampled case.

actions: Independently assign a root-cause code to each sampled case from the investigation notes.
Compare to the code recorded on the case.
testing.done: coding agreement or a documented mismatch exists for every sampled case.

actions: Independently re-run the 3-in-90-days cluster logic against the quarter's population.
Compare the result to the remediation items opened.
testing.done: any missed cluster is identified as an exception.

testing.step: Trace remediation items to closure evidence
actions: For each remediation item touching a sampled case, confirm an owner, target date and closure evidence exist.
testing.done: every sampled remediation item has complete closure evidence.

actions: Confirm each FEMA-referred sampled case shows the referral number.
Confirm the response went through the FEMA-specified channel.
testing.done: referral number and correct channel are confirmed for every sampled FEMA case.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise an issue per exception with root cause, owner and remediation date.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and date.

actions: Compute the missed-window rate against the threshold.
Write the conclusion; have the independent reviewer sign.
Report to the Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Scope the audit universe of flood notices

checklist.step: Compare each template against its required-content checklist

checklist.step: Draw the transactional sample

Record the seed and selection date.

checklist.step: Verify content accuracy on sampled notices

checklist.done: content accuracy is confirmed or logged as a finding for every sampled notice.

checklist.done: timing is recomputed and compared to the actual send date for every sampled notice.

checklist.done: delivery evidence is confirmed present for every sampled notice or logged as a gap.

Attach supporting evidence.

checklist.step: Obtain management response and action plans

checklist.step: Quality-review the workpapers

checklist.step: Track findings to closure

checklist.done: the audit record is filed and retention-labelled.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual cycle that brings every governance policy (Code of Conduct, Enterprise Risk Management policy, Compliance policy, WYO flood-program oversight policy) to the Board for review and approval.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — policy scope checked against 44 CFR 62.23(i)(1)/Claims Manual obligations and 44 CFR 62.24(c) WYO participation criteria, plus the domiciliary state's corporate-governance expectations, at each annual cycle.

In-scope processes.value: Annual identification, redline, executive review and Board approval of every governance policy touching WYO/flood-program oversight, risk and compliance.

In-scope systems.value: Policy drafts, redlines, approval votes and the approved-policy library maintained in the board portal.

Compliance procedure documented.value: Annual Governance Policy Review & Approval Procedure — inventory, owner review, redline, legal check, Board approval, publication.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by General Counsel; reviewed annually as part of the same cycle it governs.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Every in-scope policy must be re-approved, or affirmatively continued, within 12 months of its last Board approval date.

Deadline reminders configured.value: Board portal alerts the Board Governance Lead 90/60/30 days before any policy's 12-month approval anniversary.

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Approved policy versions and Board approval votes retained permanently in the board portal and mirrored to the compliance evidence repository.

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A policy that lapses past its 12-month approval anniversary is logged as a governance exception with an interim-effectiveness decision.

Remediation sign-off captured.value: General Counsel signs off on the interim-effectiveness decision and confirms it is cured at the next scheduled Board meeting.

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All governance policies in the approved-policy library with an approval anniversary falling in the review period.

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance for a policy operating past its 12-month approval anniversary without a Board decision on file.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Annual obligation tested annually against the full policy library.

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer did not draft or present any sampled policy to the Board.

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual governance-policy test workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Approved-policy library extract with version and approval-date history, producible within 5 business days of a regulator request.

Regulator response path.value: Board Governance Lead owns assembling the response; General Counsel clears it before release.

checklist.step: Inventory the governance policy library and anniversaries
actions: Pull every governance policy from the board portal library.
List each policy's last Board approval date and 12-month anniversary.
Flag policies due in the next quarter.
checklist.done: a complete inventory with approval anniversaries and due-for-review flags exists.

checklist.step: Assign owners for redline review
actions: Assign each policy to its content owner (Head of Compliance for the Compliance policy, Chief Risk Officer for the ERM policy, General Counsel for the Code of Conduct).
Set a redline-due date ahead of the anniversary.
checklist.done: every policy has a named owner and a redline-due date.

checklist.step: Redline each policy against current requirements
actions: Compare the current policy text to any regulatory change, e.g., a new Claims Manual bulletin affecting the WYO oversight policy.
Mark up changes with tracked changes in the board portal.
checklist.done: a tracked-changes redline exists for every policy due for review.

checklist.step: Legal review of redlines
actions: Review each redline for legal sufficiency and consistency with other governance documents.
Approve or return with comments.
checklist.done: every redline has a documented legal review outcome.

checklist.step: Route redlines through executive review
actions: Circulate approved redlines to the relevant executive (Head of Compliance, Chief Risk Officer, Chief HR Officer) for sign-off before Board presentation.
checklist.done: executive sign-off is on file for every redline before Board presentation.

checklist.step: Build the Board meeting policy package
actions: Compile the redlined policies, executive sign-offs and a summary of changes into the board meeting materials.
Distribute at least 5 business days ahead of the meeting.
checklist.done: the policy package is distributed at least 5 business days before the meeting.

checklist.step: Present policies for Board discussion
actions: Present each policy's material changes at the scheduled Board meeting.
Capture Board questions and requested revisions.
checklist.done: presentation and any requested revisions are documented in the meeting record.

checklist.step: Incorporate requested revisions
actions: Revise the policy per Board feedback.
Re-route the policy for a follow-up vote if the Board did not approve it on first presentation.
checklist.done: revised policies are re-routed and re-presented until approved.

checklist.step: Record the Board approval vote
actions: Record the vote (unanimous/majority, abstentions, dissents) in the minutes.
Capture the approval date on the policy record.
checklist.done: the vote and approval date are recorded in the minutes and on the policy record.

checklist.step: Publish the approved policy
actions: Version the approved policy.
Publish it to the board portal's approved-policy library.
Retire the prior version with a superseded flag.
checklist.done: the new version is published and the prior version is flagged superseded.

checklist.step: Communicate the approved policy to affected staff
actions: Notify affected teams (Compliance, Claims, Risk) of the updated policy and any operational change required.
Confirm acknowledgment where required.
checklist.done: affected teams are notified with acknowledgment tracked where required.

checklist.step: Handle a policy that misses its anniversary
actions: Where a redline is not ready in time, document an interim-effectiveness decision continuing the current policy.
Set a cure date at the next scheduled Board meeting.
checklist.done: any missed anniversary has a documented interim decision and cure date.

checklist.step: Log exceptions with disposition
actions: Log any lapsed policy or missed step as an exception with root cause and cure date.
checklist.done: every exception is logged with a cure date.

checklist.step: Retain the approval record
actions: File the redline, executive sign-off, meeting materials and minutes excerpt for each approved policy in the compliance evidence repository as well as the board portal.
checklist.done: the full approval record is retained in both systems.

checklist.step: Report policy governance status
actions: Prepare a summary of policies approved, pending and lapsed.
Present the summary to the Compliance Committee.
checklist.done: the summary reaches the Compliance Committee.
